layout_dets.text: OCTA-500: A Retinal Dataset for Optical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Coherence Tomography Angiography Study

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mingchao Li, Kun Huang, Qiuzhuo Xu, Jiadong Yang, Yuhan Zhang, Zexuan Ji, Keren Xie,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Songtao Yuan, Qinghuai Liu, and Qiang Chen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract—Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) is a novel imaging modality that has been widely utilized in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ophthalmology and neuroscience studies to observe retinal vessels and microvascular systems. However, publicly available OCTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets remain scarce. In this paper, we introduce the largest and most comprehensive OCTA dataset dubbed OCTA-500, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contains OCTA imaging under two fields of view (FOVs) from 500 subjects. The dataset provides rich images and annotations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: including two modalities (OCT/OCTA volumes), six types of projections, four types of text labels (age / gender / eye / disease)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and seven types of segmentation labels (large vessel/capillary/artery/vein/2D FAZ/3D FAZ/retinal layers). Then, we propose a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multi-object segmentation task called CAVF, which integrates capillary segmentation, artery segmentation, vein segmentation,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and FAZ segmentation under a unified framework. In addition, we optimize the 3D-to-2D image projection network (IPN) to IPN-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: V2 to serve as one of the segmentation baselines. Experimental results demonstrate that IPN-V2 achieves an ~10% mloU

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improvement over IPN on CAVF task. Finally, we further study the impact of several dataset characteristics: the training set size,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the model input (OCT/OCTA, 3D volume/2D projection), the baseline networks, and the diseases. The dataset and code are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: publicly available at: https://ieee-dataport.org/open-access/octa-500.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Keywords—Medical image dataset, retina, OCTA, segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is one of the most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: significant advances in retinal imaging, as it noninvasively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: captures 3D structural data of the retina with micron-level

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution (Huang et al., 1991). OCT is widely used to ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: serve the cross-sectional structure of the retina and moni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tor fluid leakage (Sakata et al., 2009). However, the limita-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion of OCT is that it cannot directly provide blood flow

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information. Building on the OCT platform, OCT angi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ography (OCTA) has been developed as a new useful im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aging modality for providing functional information on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retinal blood vessels and microvascular systems.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA measures the amplitude and delay of reflected or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: backscattered light in an interferometrical manner to ac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quire retinal angiography volume (Kashani et al., 2017).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The OCTA volumetric data can be projected from different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retinal layers to enable separate visualization of the corre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sponding retinal plexuses. This unique observation per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spective improves our understanding of the pathophysiol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ogy of retinal vasculature. Since its first commercial prod-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: uct in 2014, OCTA has quickly demonstrated its excellence

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the clinical application of age-related macular degener-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ation, diabetic retinopathy, choroidal neovascularization,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: glaucoma, and other eye diseases (Kashani et al., 2017;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Spaide et al., 2018; Laíns et al., 2021). More recently, OCTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has also been used to study the functional changes in reti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nal blood flow in neurological diseases, such as Alzhei-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mer's disease (Jiang et al., 2018; Zabel et al., 2019), Parkin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: son's disease (Kwapong et al., 2018; Robbin et al., 2022),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Huntington's disease (Maio et al., 2021).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Quantitative OCTA analysis of retinal vasculature is es-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sential to standardize objective interpretations of clinical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outcomes (Yao et al., 2020). Quantitative indicators, includ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing vessel density, vessel diameter index, vessel length

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fraction, vessel fractal dimension, foveal avascular zone

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (FAZ) area, and foveal avascular zone perimeter have been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: established for objective OCTA assessment (Wang et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2021). To calculate these indicators, it is necessary to seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment the vascular structures in OCTA images. OCTA seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation technology has achieved encouraging advances

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in recent years (Meiburger et al., 2021), especially in vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation (Stefan and Lee, 2020; Li et al., 2020a; Giarra-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tano et al., 2020; Mou et al., 2021) and FAZ segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Li et al., 2020a; Díaz et al., 2019; Guo et al., 2019a), also due

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to technological advances, especially deep learning. De-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spite these achievements, the quantification method of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA is still in development. With the emergence of some

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: new discoveries, the quantification methods are still being

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improved. For example, differential artery-vein analysis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has recently been demonstrated to improve OCTA perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance for objective detection and classification of eye dis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ease (Alam et al., 2019; Alam et al., 2018), thus making seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation of arteries and veins in OCTA images a new re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: search direction (Alam et al., 2020). More recently, the FAZ

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volume was proposed to depict the 3D structure of the FAZ

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Xu et al., 2021), so 3D FAZ segmentation is also a new fo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cus (Xu et al., 2022).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Datasets play a crucial role in computer vision research

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Deng et al., 2009). Over the past two decades, we have wit-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nessed tremendous advancements in fundus image research

layout_dets.text: using public datasets (Owen et al., 2009; Staal et al., 2004;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hoover et al., 2002). Due to the late start of OCTA, available

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA datasets are few and small. Image sources from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA imaging remain precious and scarce. The limited size

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of currently available datasets is a major challenging factor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Yao et al., 2020). We summarize four available OCTA da-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasets (Giarratano et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2020; Díaz et al., 2019;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Agarwal et al., 2020) in Table 1, which has the following lim-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: itations: (1) The number of images and the disease diversity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are limited. (2) The datasets are single-modality, and the da-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasets only provide OCTA projection maps. 3D volumes of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCT and OCTA are rare and urgently needed by researchers.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (3) The datasets are single-task datasets, providing only one

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: type of label. The dedicated study for a single task is com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mendable. Nevertheless, it is necessary to integrate the stud-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ies. (4) The latest foci, such as 3D FAZ segmentation and ar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tery-vein segmentation, have no available public datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To address these limitations and guide OCTA research

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forward, we introduce a new well-organized OCTA dataset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: named OCTA-500. Fig. 1 shows the content and organiza-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion of OCTA-500. The images for this dataset were col-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lected by an OCTA device from 500 subjects. The dataset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provides rich images and annotations including two fields

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of view (FOVs, 6 mm/3 mm), two modalities (OCT/OCTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volumes, 361,600 scans), six types of projections, four types

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of text labels (age/gender/eye/disease) and seven types of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation labels (large vessel/capillary/artery/vein/2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FAZ/3D FAZ/retinal layers). This dataset is one of the few

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that contain OCT/OCTA volumes. The size of OCTA-500

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (>80 GB) far exceeds that of other OCTA datasets (<0.2 GB

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Giarratano et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2020; Díaz et al., 2019;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Agarwal et al., 2020). The segmentation labels we anno-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tated can be used to explore the possible performance im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provement and space optimization brought by multi-task

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: collaboration. Among these labels, artery labels, vein labels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 3D FAZ labels in OCTA images are given publicly for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the first time. Without any exaggeration, OCTA-500 is cur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rently the largest and most comprehensive OCTA dataset.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Based on the segmentation annotations in OCTA-500,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we propose a novel multi-object segmentation task, called

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CAVF, which integrates capillary segmentation, artery seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation, vein segmentation, and FAZ segmentation un-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: der a unified framework. The proposed CAVF will bring

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convenience in the computation of quantitative indicators

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the evaluation of model performance. Focusing on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CAVF task, several state-of-the-art 2D segmentation net-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: works were selected as baselines. In addition to 2D seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation networks, we also considered the 3D-to-2D seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation method image projection network (IPN) (Li et

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: al., 2020a). To achieve competitive segmentation perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance, we further optimized the IPN to IPN-V2, to serve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as one of the 3D-to-2D segmentation baselines for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CAVF task.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: By means of a series of experiments on OCTA-500, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: address several questions: How much do deep learning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods improve with an increased amount of training

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data? How do different modality inputs affect segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion quality? Which baselines perform well on the CAVF

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: task? How well do segmentation models perform in differ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ent diseases?

layout_dets.text: 2 RELATED WORK

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1 OCTA Dataset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Over the past two decades, the continuous emergence of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: color fundus image datasets, such as CHASE (Owen et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2009), DRIVE (Staal et al., 2004), and STARE (Hoover et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2002), has stimulated enthusiasm for retinal research.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA is a relatively novel imaging modality. Due to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: late start, only a small number of OCTA datasets are pub-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: licly available thus far. See Table 1 for an overview of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: current public OCTA datasets. Giarratano (Giarratano et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2020) and ROSE (Ma et al., 2020) were used for vessel seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation, while OCTAGON (Díaz et al., 2019) and FAZID

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Agarwal et al., 2020) were used for FAZ segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These existing datasets focus on a single specific task, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: no multi-task OCTA dataset has yet been published.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In terms of data diversity, we focus on imaging modality

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (OCT/OCTA), data structure (3D volumes/projection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maps), and field of view (FOV, 6 mm/3 mm). Giarratano,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ROSE, OCTAGON, and FAZID are all single-modality da-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasets. They contain only OCTA modality, to be precise,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only projection maps of OCTA. ROSE-1 and OCTAGON

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: include superficial and deep projection maps, while Giar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ratano and FAZID only include superficial projection maps.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These projection maps are generated from 3D OCTA vol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: umes, and OCTA volumes are derived from OCT volumes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Jia et al., 2012). Multiple modalities and 3D volume data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are required in many OCTA studies (Li et al., 2020a; Xu et

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: al., 2022; Vogl et al., 2017; Jia et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2016;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Zhang et al., 2020; Lee et al., 2019; Yang et al., 2020; Zhang

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2017). Regrettably, none of these studies contain OCT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modality and 3D volume data. In FOV, OCTAGON in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cludes both 6 mm ×6 mm and 3 mm × 3 mm FOVs, while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: others contain only 3 mm × 3 mm FOV.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Disease diversity is another important aspect. Disease

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: samples can better reflect the generalization performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of different methods, so datasets with disease diversity can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be more widely used. FAZID had the largest number of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subjects (= 304) in the existing dataset, but it contains only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two diseases, diabetic retinopathy (DR) and myopia.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ROSE-2 contains various macular diseases, but the disease

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: label for each image is not explicitly given. OCTAGON

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contains only DR data. Giarratano considers only normal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cases and does not include subjects with any diseases.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Some common retinal diseases, such as age-related macu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lar degeneration (AMD), choroidal neovascularization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (CNV), central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC), retinal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vein occlusion (RVO), etc., are not included in the existing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.2 Vessel Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We have also witnessed impressive achievements in retinal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: blood vessel segmentation for color fundus images (Moc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cia et al., 2018; Mookiah et al., 2021; Fraz et al., 2012). The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA imaging modality allows visualization of the micro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vasculature (Kashani et al., 2017) and has been considered

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a powerful tool to observe retinal vessels (Spaide et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2018). Vessel segmentation in OCTA presents a series of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenges due to noise, poor contrast, low resolution, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high vessel complexity (Mou et al., 2021; Ma et al., 2020).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Nonetheless, benefiting from the inheritance of previous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel segmentation methods on color fundus images and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the development of deep learning techniques, vessel seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation in OCTA images has achieved rapid develop-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment in recent years.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Vessel segmentation methods in OCTA images can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: divided into threshold-based, filtering-based, active con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tour model-based, and deep learning-based methods.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Threshold-based methods commonly used in OCTA im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages are summarized by Terheyden et al. (2019) and Mehta

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. (2020). The vasculature has a higher signal intensity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than background tissues in OCTA images, so using a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: threshold can simply separate blood vessels and back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: grounds. However, as mentioned in (Li et al., 2017), an ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vious weakness of threshold-based methods is their intol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erance to background noise. Filtering methods have thus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been considered for noise suppression and vessel enhance-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment. In studies (Chu et al., 2016; Xu et al., 2019; Aharony

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2019), a Frangi filter (Frangi et al., 1998) was applied

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to enhance blood vessels, and then different threshold-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based methods were used to obtain vessel binary images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Li et al. (2017) adopted top-hat enhancement and optimally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: oriented flux (OOF) for small vessel detection. Threshold-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based and filter-based methods can roughly segment ves-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sels for estimating vessel density and vessel skeleton den-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sity (Terheyden et al., 2019). However, their segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: usually performs poorly in the presence of artifacts, mo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion blur, weak contrast, low resolution, and disease (Mou

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2019). In addition, specific structures such as capil-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: laries, arteries, and veins are also difficult to discrimina-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tively segment due to their lack of sufficient recognition ca-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pabilities.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Recently, the use of deep learning frameworks has stim-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ulated the rapid development of vessel segmentation algo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rithms. U-Net (Ronneberger et al., 2015) is a typical en-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coder-decoder structure with multiscale feature represen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation and is used by several works (Giarratano et al., 2020;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mou et al., 2021; Pissas et al., 2020; Lo et al., 2020) for vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation in OCTA images. The CS-Net proposed by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mou et al. (2021) supplements a spatial attention module

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and a channel attention module in the U-Net structure and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was used to segment the blood vessel skeleton in OCTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images. Giarratano et al. (2020) compared 8 different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thresholding, filtering, and deep learning methods on a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: small dataset with 55 region of interest (ROI) slices. They

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: showed that U-Net and CS-Net achieve the best perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance (Dice = 0.89) and OOF is the best filter (Dice= 0.86)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on their capillary segmentation task. Ma et al. (2020) more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recently presented OCTA-Net with two split-based stages

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to detect thick and thin vessels separately. The above meth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ods focus on segmenting 2D projection maps, whose gen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eration relies on accurate layer segmentation. Our previ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ous work (Li et al., 2020a) introduced an image projection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network (IPN), which provides a 3D-to-2D segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approach to segment 2D large vessels from 3D OCTA vol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: umes. This method does not require the use of layer seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation to generate a 2D projection map. Based on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IPN structure, the recent works PAENet (Wu et al., 2021)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and PRSNet (Li et al., 2022c) supplement the quadruple at-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tention module and dual-way projection learning module

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: respectively.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In addition to segmenting vessels with different calibers,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Alam et al. (2018, 2019) also showed that artery-vein seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation in OCTA images is feasible and a potential re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: search direction. They used a fully convolutional network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: named AV-Net (Alam et al., 2020) to segment the arteries

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and veins in OCTA images. However, due to the lack of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: public annotations, artery-vein segmentation in OCTA im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages has not been widely developed. To fill this vacancy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and stimulate its development, the artery-vein segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion annotations are included in the OCTA-500 dataset.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.3 FAZ Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The foveal avascular zone (FAZ) is a nonperfused region of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the fovea, which is surrounded by interconnected retinal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels. The FAZ also approximates the region of highest

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cone photoreceptor density and oxygen consumption.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Over the last decade, the FAZ has often been analyzed un-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: der different aspects, mainly by fluorescence angiography

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (FA) (Conrath et al., 2005; Zheng et al., 2010). The novel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA technology allows a noninvasive examination,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: visualization and quantitative analysis of the FAZ. Several

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: new findings in OCTA reveal that the size of the FAZ is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: highly correlated with both visual acuity and disease

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Freiberg et al., 2016; Balaratnasingam, 2016). Hence, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FAZ has received increasing attention from clinicians and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: researchers, and its segmentation has become a focus in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA studies. Quantitative evaluation of the FAZ area and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: perimeter relies on FAZ segmentation. FAZ segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is also used to locate the foveal center (Li, 2020b). A more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recent study (Lin et al., 2021) also shows that the features

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in FAZ segmentation can also be used to improve the per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formance of multi-disease classification.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Current FAZ segmentation methods can be divided into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unsupervised methods and supervised methods. The un-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supervised methods are designed according to the location

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: characteristics (located at the imaging center), geometric

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: characteristics (unique connected area) and gray character-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: istics (no vessel) of the FAZ. They often need to set the ini-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tial seed or initial contour. For example, Lu et al. (2018) pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sented a generalized gradient vector flow (GGVF) snake

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model to evolve the FAZ contour through an initial circular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: area. Xu et al. (2019) determined initial seeds in distance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transform images and then used a graph cut to finish seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation. These unsupervised methods could have excel-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lent performance on a small dataset with a healthy or sin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gle disease but might encounter more difficulties when ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plied to larger and more complex datasets (Guo et al., 2021).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Deep learning techniques have demonstrated an excellent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ability to determine the complex structure of high-dimen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sional data. Many deep learning methods have been re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ported for FAZ segmentation. The U-Net backboned en-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coder-decoder structure is currently the most used net-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work architecture in the FAZ segmentation task and has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been adopted by many works (Guo et al., 2019b, 2021; Li et

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: al., 2020b; Guo et al., 2018, 2019a; Liang et al., 2021; Jabour

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2021) for end-to-end FAZ segmentation on 2D OCTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: projection maps (enface OCTA). Mirshahi et al. (2021) used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mask R-CNN for FAZ segmentation on enface OCTA im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages. Our previous work also performed 3D-to-2D FAZ

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation by using IPN (Li et al., 2020a). Xu et al. (2021)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more recently proposed a new index, FAZ volume. To cal-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: culate the FAZ volume, they developed a 3D U-Net struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture to segment the 3D FAZ (Xu et al., 2022). It is worth

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentioning that both 2D and 3D FAZ annotations are in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cluded in OCTA-500. More related works on vessel seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation and FAZ segmentation are summarized in Ta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bles S1 and S2 in Supplementary Material

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.4 Main Contributions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our contributions are threefold:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We introduce the OCTA-500 dataset, which con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tains OCTA imaging under two FOVs from 500

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subjects. The OCTA-500 dataset provides rich im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages and annotations including 2 modalities

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (OCT/OCTA volumes), 6 projections, 4 text labels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (age/gender/eye/disease), and 7 segmentation la-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bels(largevessel/capillary/artery/vein/2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FAZ/3D FAZ/retinal layers). It is currently the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: most comprehensive OCTA dataset. See Section 3.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We propose a CAVF task that integrates artery

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation, vein segmentation, capillary seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation, and FAZ segmentation under a uni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fied framework. Based on the CAVF task, we op-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: timize the 3D-to-2D network IPN to IPN-V2 to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: serve as one of the competitive baselines. See Sec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion 4.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We provide insights into several dataset charac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teristics: the training set size, the model input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (OCT/OCTA, 3D volume/2D projection), the base-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lines (2D-to-2D baselines/3D-to-2D baselines),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the diseases. See Section 5.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3 OCTA-500 DATASET

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this section, we first introduce the data collection pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cess and the two subsets of the OCTA-500 (Section 3.1); we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: then introduce the contents of the OCTA-500 including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCT/OCTA volumes (Section 3.2), projection maps (Sec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion 3.3), text labels (Section 3.4) and segmentation labels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Section 3.5).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1 Data Collection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA-500 contains a total of 500 subjects divided into two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subsets according to the FOV type: OCTA_6mm and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA_3mm. OCTA_6mm includes 300 subjects (NO.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 10001 - NO. 10300) who underwent macular OCT/OCTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imaging with a FOV of 6 mm × 6 mm. OCTA_3mm in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cludes 200 subjects (NO. 10301 - NO. 10500) who under-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: went macular OCT/OCTA imaging with an FOV of 3 mm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: × 3 mm. The OCT/OCTA images are from the same device,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is a commercial 70 kHz spectral-domain OCT sys-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tem with a center wavelength of 840 nm (RTVue-XR,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Optovue, CA). All subjects were imaged at Jiangsu Prov-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ince Hospital from March 2018 to July 2020. To ensure pa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tient independence, only one eye of each subject was in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cluded. The registration information of all subjects was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: complete, and the type of diagnosed disease was given by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ophthalmologists. OCTA_6mm and OCTA_3mm came

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from two independent recruitments and therefore differed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in disease diversity. The subjects of OCTA_6mm are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mainly from a population with common retinal diseases,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the normal population is a minority. The subjects of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA_3mm are mainly from the normal population, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: secondarily from the diseased population. More details

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: about the disease distribution can be found in Section 3.4.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2 OCT and OCTA Volumes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The OCTA-500 dataset contains volume data of two mo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dalities, OCT and OCTA volumes, as shown in Fig. 2. OCT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volumes and OCTA volumes provide structural infor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mation and blood flow information of the retina, respec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tively. The OCTA volume is generated from OCT volumes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by the split-spectrum amplitude-decorrelation angi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ography (SSADA) algorithm (Jia et al., 2012). Due to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: use of band-pass filtering and split-spectrum methods in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the SSADA algorithm, the vertical resolution of the OCTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volume is 1/4 of the OCT volume. We used bilinear inter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: polation to resize it, and then the OCT and OCTA volumes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were registered. The FOV and resolution of the two subsets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are different. The imaging range of OCTA_6mm is 6m m ×

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6 mm × 2 mm centered on the fovea, and its volume size is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 2. 3D visualization of the OCT volumes and OCTA volumes in two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fields of view.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 400 px × 400 px × 640 px. The imaging range of OCTA_3mm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is 3 mm × 3 mm × 2 mm centered on the fovea, and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volume size is 304 px × 304 px × 640 px. For ease of reading

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by researchers, we present these 3D volumes in the form of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2D scans (B-scans), for a total of 361,600 scans.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.3 Projection Maps

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The provision of 3D OCT/OCTA volumes allows us to sep-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: arately project and visualize different retinal layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: through layer segmentation. In OCTA-500, we provide six

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: types of projection maps, as shown in Fig. 3. We used the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retinal layer position information of the internal limiting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: membrane (ILM) layer, the outer plexiform layer (OPL)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Bruch's membrane (BM). Two kinds of projection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods are selected for the generation of projection maps:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: average projection and maximum projection. These projec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion methods are obtained by averaging or maximizing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: along the axial direction. The OCT volume usually uses the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: average projection. Since the value in OCTA volume re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flects the intensity of the blood flow signal, to show the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shape of blood vessels more clearly, the maximum projec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion is usually used in the projection maps of the inner ret-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ina and outer retina (Hormel et al., 2018). The projection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maps we generated are as follows:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (B1) OCT full projection, the average value of 3D OCT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volume along the axial direction, which shows the global

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information of the OCT volume. OCT full projection is of-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ten used to observe retinal vessels and edema (Vogl et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (B2) OCT average projection between the ILM and OPL.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It can show the vessels in the inner retina with high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 3. Generation of the projection maps. (A1-A2) A B-scan of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OČT/OCTA and the layer segmentation used. (B1-B3) OCT projection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (B4-B6) OCTA projection. The table lists the modality, projection re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gion and projection mode of each projection map.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reflection (Chen et al., 2016).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (B3) OCT average projection between the OPL and BM.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It displays the vessel shadows in the outer retina with low

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reflection. It shows higher vessel contrast than the B2 pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jection (Chen et al., 2016).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (B4) OCTA full projection. It is the average value of 3D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA volume along the axial direction, which is a global

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: view of both the retina and choroid.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (B5) OCTA maximum projection between the ILM and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OPL. It is generated by the maximum projection of the in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ner retina which can clearly show the vāscular morphology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the inner retina (Li et al., 2020a) and the shape of the FAZ

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Lu et al., 2018).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (B6) OCTA maximum projection between the OPL and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: BM. It is generated by the maximum projection of the outer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retina, which can be used to observe and monitor the mor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phology of CNV (Jia et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2016).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Note that the projection maps we have given above are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: common, but not all. We also provide layer segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotations (see details in Section 3.5.5) so that researchers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can generate projection maps according to their needs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.5 Segmentation Labels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this section, we introduce the labeling criteria and pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cesses of the segmentation labels in OCTA-500, including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: large vessel, artery, vein, capillary, 2D/3D FAZ, and retinal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layers.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.5.1 Large Vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: There have been many applications for segmenting large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels in OCTA images. For example, the vessel density of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: large vessels is an important indicator in assessing retinal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: disease (Xu et al., 2019). Large vessels can be used as a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask to remove artifacts, which is a necessary step for seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: menting capillaries in OCTA images (Jiang et al., 2018; Xu

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2019; Li et al., 2017). In Section 3.5.2, we also show

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that large vessels can be further differentiated into arteries

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and veins, motivating further development of the vascular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assessment. In this section, we will introduce how we ac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: curately label such important large vessels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Large vessels are distributed in the inner retina, show-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing a high-intensity tree-shaped structure in OCTA projec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion map B5 (Fig. 5a). The signal intensity of large vessels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is generally slightly higher than that of capillaries. How-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ever, it is still difficult to segment it accurately only by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: threshold binarization. Fig. 5e shows the result of segment-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing large vessels with threshold binarization, which still re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tains capillaries and noise. To obtain accurate and clean

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: large vessel segmentation labels, we perform manual label-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing of large vessels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We used Adobe Photoshop CC (Adobe Systems, Inc.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: San Jose, CA, USA) to annotate the large vessel in projec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion map B5. The labeling process is divided into two steps:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coarse-grained annotation and fine-grained correction. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the coarse-grained annotation stage, we draw the large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels using a red brush (R: 255, G: 0, B: 0, hardness: 100)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on a separate layer. The thickness of the brush is larger than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the diameter of the blood vessel. In this stage, we do not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pursue the precise boundary, but ensure that there are no

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: missing blood vessels. The result of this annotation stage

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has a thicker vessel diameter, as shown in Fig. 5b. We then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 5. Annotation of the large vessels in OCTA-500. (a) OCTA projec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion map (B5). (b) Coarse-grained manual annotation. (c) Visualization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of coarse-grained annotation in ‘Screen' mode. (d) Fine-grained man-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ual corrections in ‘Screen' mode. (e) Threshold result. (f) The final la-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bel of large vessels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performed fine-grained correction delicately delineate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel boundaries. In this time, we used the 'Screen' mode,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in which the over-segmented part will appear red with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: higher saturation (Fig. 5c, yellow arrow). We finely deline-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ated the boundary so that the shape of the blood vessels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was consistent with the gray distribution in the projection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: map, and at the same time, the smoothness and continuity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the blood vessels were also ensured (Fig. 5d). Return to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: "normal" mode, adjust the color, and obtain the final large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel label (Fig. 5f).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.5.2 Artery and Vein

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Large vessels can be further divided into arteries and veins.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Differential artery-vein analysis can provide valuable in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formation for evaluating ophthalmic diseases and improv-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing the performance of disease classification (Alam et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2019a). At present, very few studies segment arteries and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: veins in OCTA images. Alam et al. (2018, 2019a, 2019b) re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cently demonstrated the potential of differentiating arter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ies and veins in OCTA. One of their key proposals is to use

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: color fundus images as a guide to distinguish between ar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teries and veins in OCTA images. Indeed, even for human

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experts, it is difficult to manually annotate arteries and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: veins using only OCTA images. To improve the efficiency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and accuracy of artery-vein annotation, we refer to multi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ple imaging modalities, including color fundus images,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCT, and OCTA.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We divide the manually annotated large vessels into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 6. Annotation of the arteries and veins in OCTA-500. (a) Color

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fundus image. (b) The mean results of models trained on an extra da-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taset. (c) OCTA projection map (B5). (d) OCT projection map (B3).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Blue circles represent branch points and yellow circles represent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crossover points. (e) The large vessel label. (f) The final artery-vein

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: label. Red represents arteries. Green represents veins.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: arteries and veins. To this end, we first determined the ar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: terial and venous categories of the main vessels on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: color fundus images (Fig. 6a). Annotation guidelines can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be found in (Kondermann et al., 2007). Compared with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCT/OCTA, color fundus images present a wider field of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: view and have color information, making it easier to dis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tinguish between arteries and veins. However, using only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: color fundus images cannot label the arteriovenous prop-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erties of all large vessels because of the limited ability of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: color fundus images to image vessel branches. We then de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: termined the arteriovenous properties of each vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branch by identifying vessel crossover points and branch

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: points in OCTA projection maps B5 (Fig. 6c) and B3 (Fig.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6d). The guidelines of the crossover points and branch

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: points are as follows: The branch point is 3-branched and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the crossover point is 4-branched; The crossover points

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: usually have a darker color (Fig. 6c, yellow box), and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branch points are more consistent in color (Fig. 6c, blue

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: box); Vessel properties at branch points are consistent; Ves-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sels with the same property generally do not intersect,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which means that the two cross vessels are generally con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tain one artery and one vein.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The properties of the main blood vessels were deter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mined by the color fundus images, and the crossover and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branch points were determined by the OCT/OCTA projec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion maps. Combining the two, the large vessels annotated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 7. Annotation of the capillary in OCTA-500. (A) An example of manual annotation from ROSE-1. (B) Examples of manual annotation in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Giarratano. (C) Examples of manual labeling of OCTA-500 slices. (D) Capillary labeling process in OCTA-500: (1) OCTA projection map (B5).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (2) The preliminary segmentation result using IMN. (3) The result of topology optimization and denoising using LAL. (4) The final label. Blue

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: represents the large vessels. White represents the capillaries.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Section 3.5.1 (Fig. 6e) can be further marked as arteries

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and veins.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Numerous subjects in the OCTA-500 were unable to dis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tinguish the arteriovenous properties of the main vessels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: due to the lack of corresponding color fundus images. To

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: remedy this lack, we trained the deep models on an extra

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: private dataset, which contains 100 subjects with color fun-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dus images and OCT/OCTA images. Arteries and veins are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labeled following the above guidelines. We trained three

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models U-Net (Ronneberger et al., 2015), U-Net++ (Zhou et

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: al., 2018), Attention U-Net (Oktay et al., 2018), and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mean result is shown in Fig. 6b. This mean result has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: very close to the real situation, but to ensure the reliability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the labeling, this result is used only to discriminate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properties of the main vessels. Nevertheless, the branch

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels are determined by the crossover points and branch

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: points. In this way, we labeled the vast majority of large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel labels as artery labels and vein labels (Fig. 6f), but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some vessels with relatively small calibers that could not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be identified as arteries and veins were excluded.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.5.3 Capillary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Capillaries appear as a dense mesh structure in OCTA im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages. Manual annotating capillaries in OCTA images is ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tremely time-consuming, and limited image resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the presence of noise make it nearly impossible to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: manually label all capillaries in the entire image. For this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reason, currently supervised vessel segmentation methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: focus mainly on large vessels with limited capillary anno-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation. An example of ROSE-1 (Ma et al., 2020) is given in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 7A. We can see that numerous capillaries are still un-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: der-labeled, and their labeling of capillaries is skeleton-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: level. To obtain a more complete capillary label at the pixel-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: level, we followed the work of Giarratano et al. (2020).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: They cropped 55 ROI slices with 91 × 91 pixels on OCTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: projection maps and performed detailed large vessel and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capillary annotation (Fig. 7B). Through training, testing,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and stitching, complete full-vessel segmentation can be ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tained.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this work, we randomly cropped 100 slices with 76 ×

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 76 pixels from the projection map B5 in OCTA-500. The ca-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pillaries in these slices were then manually annotated (Fig.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 7C). These annotated slices and the slices in the dataset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Giarratano et al., 2020) were both used as training data.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We trained the segmentation model using our previously

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed image magnification network (IMN) (Li et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2022a). This network structure can well preserve image de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tails, which is dedicated to capillary segmentation. Using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the trained IMN model to test the whole projection map B5

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Fig. 7D-(1)) through a sliding window, we can obtain the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: full-vessel labels (Fig. 7D-(2)). Nevertheless, this result has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: several deficiencies. On the one hand, there is still noticea-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ble image noise in the results. For example, the pixel indi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cated by the yellow arrow in the FAZ is identified as a ves-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sel, which may be related to the lack of global information

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: caused by training on the slices. On the other hand, the top-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ological clarity of capillaries still needs to be improved.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To further remove noise and improve the topological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: clarity of capillaries, we performed additional optimiza-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions on the IMN segmentation results. First, we remove

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the noise in the FAZ region using the FAZ mask provided

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Section 3.5.4. Then, we enhance the topology of blood

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels using our recently proposed label adversarial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning (LAL) (Li et al., 2022b), a skeleton-level to pixel-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: level vessel segmentation method that can realize the ad-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: justment of the blood vessel diameter and has a certain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.5.4 Foveal Avascular Zone

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the foveal region, the superficial and deep vascular plex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: uses form a special capillary-free region, the FAZ, by form-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing a ring of interconnecting capillaries at the margin of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fovea (Samara et al., 2015). According to this definition, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FAZ should be a 3D region, but at present, most quantifi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cation methods for the FAZ are mainly to segment the 2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FAZ on the projection view and calculate 2D indicators,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such as the FAZ area. The FAZ area has been found to be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: associated with visual acuity and disease (Freiberg et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2016; Balaratnasingam et al., 2016). Our recent work pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: poses the FAZ volume and gives a 3D definition of the FAZ

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Xu et al., 2021), and it shows a greater sensitivity for vas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cular alteration. In the OCTA-500 dataset, both 2D and 3D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FAZ labels are included.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We annotated the 2D FAZ in the OCTA projection map

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: B5 using Adobe Photoshop CC. The guidelines are as fol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capillaries; Separate largest closed loop. The quick selec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion tool is used to improve labeling efficiency. All annota-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion results were reviewed by multiple experts. Fig. 8b

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shows an FAZ annotation result. These FAZ labels were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: published in an earlier version of OCTA-500. In the latest

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: version, we have optimized and updated the FAZ labels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Considering the recently completed capillary labels in Sec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion 3.5.3, we found that the FAZ border did not fit per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fectly with the capillary plexus, as indicated by the yellow

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: arrow in Fig. 8c. Thus, we perform a pixel-wise optimiza-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion of the FAZ boundaries based on the capillary label, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown in Fig. 8d. This optimization considers the correla-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion of the FAZ boundary with the capillary plexus to make

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the OPL layer. The layer segmentation used is de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
