layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.5.5 Retinal Layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Layer segmentation is an important tool for analyzing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure and function of different layers in OCT/OCTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images. Retinal thickness analysis (Geobel et al., 2002), ves-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sel density statistics between different layers (Lavia et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2019), and generation of projection maps as described in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Section 3.3 all require layer segmentation. Numerous auto-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matic retinal layer segmentation algorithms have been re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ported in recent years (Li et al., 2006; Garvin et al, 2009;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Antony et al., 2011; Novosel et al., 2017; Xiang et al., 2018;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Zhang et al., 2020; Bogunovic et al., 2019; Yang et al., 2022).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Diseases can alter or destroy the retinal layers, so that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retinal layers have complex and diverse shapes under dif-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ferent diseases (Fig. 10), which further leads to the design

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of retinal layer segmentation algorithms under disease

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 10. Diversity of the segmentation labels in the OCTA-500 dataset.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diversity being still a challenging task. To motivate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layer segmentation task to move forward and to facilitate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: readers to better use OCTA-500, we release the layer seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation labels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We label 6 retinal layers, which are internal limiting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: membrane (ILM), inner plexiform layer (IPL), outer plexi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: form layer (OPL), inner segment/outer segment (ISOS), ret-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inal pigment epithelium (RPE), and Bruch's membrane

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (BM). We first obtained preliminary results for these 6 lay-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ers using Iowa software (OCTExplorer 3.8) (Li et al., 2006;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Garvin et al., 2009; Antony et al., 2011). These results are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: usually inaccurate in disease cases, so we further corrected

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the results. Fig. 9(a) shows a case of layer segmentation er-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rors under AMD disease. Three types of fluid, intraretinal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fluid (IRF), subretinal fluid (SRF), and pigment epithelial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detachment (PED), affect the layer structure in this case.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We modified the layers of this case referring to the defini-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion in (Bogunovic et al., 2019): SRF is between the neuro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sensory retina and the underlying RPE that nourishes pho-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: toreceptors. PED represents detachment of the RPE along

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the overlying retina from the remaining BM. The cor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rected result is shown in Fig. 9(b). We also refer to (Xiang

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2018; Scy et al., 2012; Staurenhi et al., 2014) for man-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ual correction of mislabels in other diseases. More exam-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ples can be seen in Fig. 10.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Since OCTA-500 contains rich diseases, the layer labels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are suitable to explore the retinal layer segmentation algo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rithm under the condition of disease diversity. As this pa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: per tends to introduce the next CAVF task, we will not ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plore the layer segmentation algorithm further. For more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: research on the layer segmentation algorithm in OCTA-500,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: please refer to (Zhang et al., 2020; Yang et al., 2022), both of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which use the data in OCTA-500.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4 CAVF TASK AND BASELINES

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.1 CAVF Task

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Based on the segmentation labels provided by our dataset,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we propose a new CAVF task, which unifies Capillary seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation, Artery segmentation, Vein segmentation, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FAZ segmentation under one framework. Fig. 10 provides

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some examples of the multi-object segmentation labels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Compared with segmenting them one by one, the pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: posed CAVF task will bring convenience in the computa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion of quantitative indicators and the evaluation of model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Understanding retinal diseases often requires quanti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tative analysis of different structural indicators (ves-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sel density, FAZ area, etc.), and the calculation of these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: indicators often relies on different segmentation tasks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Previous studies (Ma et al., 2020; Díaz et al., 2019; Xu

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2022; Pissas et al., 2020; Lo et al., 2020) focused

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on single segmentation task. Training one model per

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: task would be inconvenient for the application. Our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed multi-object segmentation task unifies sev-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eral interrelated segmentation tasks: the FAZ is sur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rounded by capillaries; arteries and veins are mutu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ally exclusive, and one vessel cannot be identified as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both an artery and a vein, etc. The proposed multi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object segmentation task allows one model to solve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multiple segmentation problems, which reduces the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computational burden and brings convenience to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: clinical applications.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Multi-objectsegmentationaggregates the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 11. Proposed IPN-V2 architecture for 3D-to-2D segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: characteristics of each individual segmentation, al-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lowing a more comprehensive evaluation of model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance. For example, capillary segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: may require the model with the ability to maintain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high-resolution information, FAZ segmentation may

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: require the model to consider the location character-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: istics of objects, and artery-vein segmentation may re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quire the model to extract higher-level features to dis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tinguish them.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.2 Baselines

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To initially explore our proposed CAVF task, we selected

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: several 2D-to-2D baselines as described in Section 4.2.1,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and optimized the 3D-to-2D baseline as described in Sec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion 4.2.2. Codes of these baselines are available in our da-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taset.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.2.1 2D-to-2D Baselines

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The 2D-to-2D baselines we selected are U-Net

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Ronneberger et al., 2015), UNet ++ (Zhou et al., 2018),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: UNet 3+ (Huang et al.,2020), Attention U-Net (Oktay et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2018), CS-Net (Mou et al., 2021), and AV-Net (Alam et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2020). Among them, U-Net is the most commonly used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolutional neural network in medical image segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion, and it has been proven to be fast and accurate, even

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with few training images. Many recent OCTA segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion methods (Mou et al., 2021; Guo et al., 2019a; Alam et

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: al., 2020; Mou et al., 2019; Pissas et al., 2020; Lo et al., 2020;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Li et al., 2020b) are extensions of U-Net and profit from the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: basic concepts of these methods. UNet ++, UNet 3+, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Attention U-Net optimize the structure and function based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on U-Net, and they are also selected as baselines. Focusing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on OCTA segmentation, we choose the baselines CS-Net

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and AV-Net, which are designed for vessel segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and artery-vein segmentation, respectively, and we tested

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their performance on our dataset. All of the above base-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lines take 2D projection images as input (the network in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: puts will be discussed in Section 5.2), and all hyperparam-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eters are tuned to yield full segmentation performance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.2.2 3D-to-2D Baselines

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our previous work (Li et al., 2020a) introduced an image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: projection network (IPN) for 3D to 2D segmentation,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which inputs 3D OCT/OCTA volumes and outputs 2D seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation results end-to-end. This 3D-to-2D segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: brings several benefits: for example, the segmentation no

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: longer needs to rely on layer segmentation to generate pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jection images, which avoids the failure of layer segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion under disease conditions; it utilizes the complete 3D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information, which reduces information loss and improves

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation performance. To explore 3D-to-2D segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation on the CAVF task, we use IPN as one of the baselines.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, it does not perform well in our experiments (see

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Section 5.2), as the CAVF task is more challenging than pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vious segmentation of large vessels or FAZ alone. Thus, in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this work, we also introduce IPN-V2 (Fig. 11), which opti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mized the structure of the IPN, to serve as one of the base-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lines.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We first point out the limitations of the IPN in two as-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pects. First, the training and testing of the IPN takes up

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: considerable GPU memory and is inefficient. Due to lim-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ited computing resources, we usually split the volume data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (with a size of 640 × 400 × 400) into small blocks (e. g. with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a size of 640 × 100 × 100) to train the IPN instead of input-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ting the whole volume data, which will lose some global

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information. Second, IPN has no down-sampling opera-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion in the horizontal direction, so it lacks high-level se-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mantic information, which is also one of the reasons for its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: poor performance on the proposed task.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To address the above limitation, we rethought the spa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tial structure of the IPN, as shown in Fig. 12. The 3D con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volution operations with a kernel size of 3×3×3 in the first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: half of the network (Fig. 12, blue box) take up the most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 12. Schematic representation of the computational space of IPN

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and IPN-V2.

layout_dets.label: display_formula
layout_dets.latex: m I o U = \frac { 1 } { k } \sum _ { i = 1 } ^ { k } I o U

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computational space. However, these convolutions in a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: large 3D space are inefficient: OCT/OCTA volumes contain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a large amount of background, and it is not necessary to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extract features in these positions. Thus, we consider first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compressing the 3D information to 2D quickly to reduce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the computational space of this part, and then further seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment the target from the extracted 2D features. Based on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the above considerations, the proposed IPN-V2 is thus de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: signed and consists of two stages: the 3D-to-2D projection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stage and the 2D segmentation stage.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3D-to-2D projection stage: This stage is mainly to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quickly compress 3D information into a 2D space. To this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: end, we design the fast projection module (FPM). As

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown in Fig. 11, the FPM includes four down-sampling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operations, which are three different scales of convolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the unidirectional pooling used in IPN. Multi-scale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolutions are used to extract and condense useful fea-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tures, and unidirectional pooling can compress features

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and make training more stable. The FPM inputs the 3D vol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ume with a size of (H, L, W) and the output volume with a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: size of (H/h, L, W), where h is the compression factor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Through several FPMs, 3D information is condensed into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a 2D space to obtain a series of 2D features.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2D segmentation stage: The obtained 2D features are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: further segmented by a 2D segmentation network to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieve the complete segmentation task. In theory, the 2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation network can use an arbitrary 2D convolu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tional neural network (CNN), such as the U-Net++ or other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2D baselines mentioned above. In this paper, to provide a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: valuable comparison, the 2D segmentation network is de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: signed as a classic encoder-decoder structure similar to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: U-Net. We also considered that IPN lacks high-level se-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mantic information. The multi-scale semantic representa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion provided by this design just overcomes this limitation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Note that, although IPN-V2 is designed to contain the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: above two stages, it is still an independent network that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be trained end-to-end. After the above optimizations,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IPN-V2 can take the entire OCT/OCTA volume as input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and achieve competitive segmentation on the CAVF task.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, IPN-V2 is considered an important 3D-to-2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation baseline. Ablation study of IPN-V2 see Sup-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plementary Materials.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.3 Evaluation Metrics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To objectively evaluate the segmentation performance of each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object in our segmentation task, the following metrics can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: calculated and compared:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1) Dice coefficient (Dice): 2TP/(2TP+FP+FN);

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2) Intersection over union (IoU): TP/(TP+FP+FN);

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3) Accuracy (ACC): (TP+TN)/(TP+FP+TN+FN);

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4) Sensitivity (SE): TP/(TP+FN);

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5) Specificity (SP): TN/(TN+FP);

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where TP is true positive, FP is false positive, TN is true neg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ative, and FN is false negative. To measure the comprehen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sive segmentation performance of the model, we use mean

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intersection over union (mIoU) as an important metric for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the proposed CAVF task, and it is denoted as:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where k is the number of segmentation objects. In addition,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we also used the number of parameters (Params), the GPU

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: memory occupied per batch (Memory) and test speed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (reading and inference time for each subject) to reflect the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computational complexity of the model.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5 EXPERIMENTS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We quantitatively and qualitatively studied the CAVF task

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the OCTA-500. We started with introducing the experi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mental setting in Section 5.1. Then, we evaluated the im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pact of several dataset characteristics: the training set size

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Section 5.2), the model input (Section 5.3), the baselines

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Section 5.4) and the diseases (Section 5.5).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5.1 Experimental Settings

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We set the training set, validation set and test set on two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subsets of OCTA-500. OCTA_6mm includes a training set

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (NO. 10001-NO. 10240), a validation set (NO. 10241-NO.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 10250), and a test set (NO. 10251-NO. 10300). OCTA_3mm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: includes a training set (NO. 10301-NO. 10440), a validation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: set (NO. 10441-NO. 10450), and a test set (NO. 10451-NO.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 10500). The training set is used to train network models;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the validation set is used to select the best model; and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: test set is used for evaluation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All baselines are implemented with PyTorch on 2

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU. Cross entropy loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Dice loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are the two most popular loss functions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in segmentation tasks, as described in (Ma et al., 2021). We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: use the unweighted sum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as the default loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: function. We train the network using Adam optimization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a batch size of 4 and an initial learning rate of 0.0005.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Each baseline iterates at least 300 epochs and saves the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model every epoch. OCT/OCTA volumes are resized to 128

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: × 400 × 400 for OCTA_6mm and 128 × 304 × 304 for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA_3mm using bilinear interpolation. Other experi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mental settings (number of training sets, types of input im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages, etc.) will be given or discussed in the following sec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5.2 Number of Training Data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We explore how the segmentation quality varies with in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creasing amount of training data. More specifically, we se-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lect the 2D-to-2D baseline U-Net and 3D-to-2D baseline

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IPN-V2 to perform experiments on the OCTA_6mm. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: input of U-Net is all projection maps as introduced in Sec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion 3.3, and the input of IPN-V2 is the OCTA volume. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training data are selected from the training set, and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluation is performed on the test set of OCTA_6mm.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The results of this experiment are shown in Fig. 13. As

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it can be observed, the mIoU increases as we increase the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: number of training data samples. Specifically, when the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: number is less than 120, the mIoU increases rapidly. When

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the number is more than 120, the increase in mIoU becomes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: less pronounced, but we can still see some subtle improve-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments from the examples. In our opinion, the sample num-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ber of 120 is a basic requirement for this task, and the sam-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ple numbers of OCTA_6mm and OCTA_3mm are 300 and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 200, respectively, which meet this requirement.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We also discuss the segmentation performance of each

layout_dets.text: 5.3 Types of Input Data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Since different types of input data have differentiated in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formation, we conducted a set of experiments to under-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stand the effectiveness of using different inputs. In this sec-

layout_dets.text: tion, we still selected the U-Net and IPN-V2 to perform ex-

layout_dets.text: quantitative metrics of these results according to the cate-

layout_dets.text: gory of the diseases. Fig. 15 shows the results and exam-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6 DISCUSSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We have demonstrated the CAVF task to achieve joint seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation of capillaries, arteries, veins, and the FAZ.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 15. Segmentation performance on different diseases using IPN-V2 on OCTA_6mm.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Segmentation labels in OCTA-500 also allow us to achieve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: large vessel segmentation, 3D FAZ segmentation, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layer segmentation. Experiments for each single segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion task are provided in the Supplementary Materials.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These tasks are not only used to optimize and evaluate al-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gorithms, but more importantly, they provide diverse reti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nal image quantification and evaluation methods, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: will play an important role in disease analysis. For exam-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ple, layer segmentation is used to calculate retinal layer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thickness (Goebel et al., 2002), vessel segmentation is used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to calculate vessel density (Livia et al., 2019), FAZ segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation is used to calculate FAZ area (Samara et al., 2015),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: etc.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA-500 also provides a variety of disease labels,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which can be used for disease classification. A recent study

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Lin et al., 2021) discussed the classification performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of normal, DR and AMD using the projection images in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA-500. Still, more diseases need to be discussed, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3D OCT/OCTA volumes have not been used. OCTA-500 is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one of the few datasets that contains paired OCT/OCTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volumes. The multi-modality data will support a wider

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: range of research, such as modality transformation (Lee et

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: al., 2019), image denoising (Yang et al., 2020), artifact re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: moval (Zhang et al., 2017), multi-modality fusion (Jia et

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: al.,2014), etc. We also expect OCTA-500 to stimulate more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interesting research topics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 7 CONCLUSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We have introduced the new OCTA-500 dataset, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contains OCTA imaging from 500 subjects and provides a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rich set of images and annotations. Based on the provided

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation annotations, we have proposed a new CAVF

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation task that integrates artery segmentation,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vein segmentation, capillary segmentation, and FAZ seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation under a unified framework. Focusing on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed CAVF task, we optimized the 3D-to-2D network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IPN to IPN-V2 to serve as one of the baselines. We have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: explored the effect of several dataset characteristics on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CAVF task: the training set size, the model input, the base-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lines, and the diseases.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The experiments show that data are a driving factor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for the segmentation performance in the proposed task.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our dataset has been at a reasonable level in terms of data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scale. The proposed IPN-V2 has improved the quality and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: speed of segmentation by a large margin compared with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IPN, and achieved competitive results. We also show that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the disease diversity of OCTA-500 increases the challenge

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the segmentation task. The considered deep learning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods have not yet been saturated in this task. Future

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improvement will come from better methods and in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creased data.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA-500 allows us to implement a variety of seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation tasks, which will provide a systematic quantita-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tive framework for retinal image analysis. We also dis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cussed its potential applications in other OCTA studies.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hence, we expect that it will stimulate research toward the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quantification, analysis and application of OCT/OCTA im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages. Our future plans are to continue collecting images,

layout_dets.text: ABLATION STUDY OF IPN-V2

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The ablation study of IPN-V2 was performed on the OCTA_6mm including the following configurations:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (i) IPN: basic IPN with 4 projection learning modules.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (ii) IPN-V2 with a CNN backbone: the 2D segmentation stage uses a standard CNN without down-sampling and con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: catenation operations. In this configuration, we aim to measure the segmentation performance in the absence of high-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: level semantic information.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (iii) IPN-V2 without FPM: the 3D-to-2D projection stage uses a single 1x1 convolution operation with stride h for down-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sampling. In this configuration, we aim to illustrate the effectiveness of FPM.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (iv) IPN-V2: the complete IPN-V2 architecture as shown in Fig.11.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The input of the above network is the OCTA volume. Since training the IPN consumes considerable GPU memory,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the entire volume (128 × 400 × 400) cannot be accommodated, the input for the above configurations is unified as a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: patch (128 × 100 × 100) randomly cropped from the OCTA volume.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The results of these experiments are shown in Table S3. It can be observed that IPN-V2 has a considerable perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance improvement compared to IPN. This improvement comes from efficient feature compression by FPM and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high-level semantics provided by U-Net, both of which are indispensable. After adding the high-dimensional semantic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information provided by U-Net, the artery segmentation, vein segmentation and FAZ segmentation are significantly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improved, which also reflects that the identification of arteries, veins and FAZ is more difficult than that of capillaries.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IPN-V2 greatly reduces GPU memory usage compared to IPN, which means that IPN-V2 allows for a larger size

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: input. We further performed additional ablation studies on the effect of increasing the input size as the following con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: figuration:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (v) IPN-V2: the complete IPN-V2 architecture with an input size of 128 × 200 × 200.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (vi) IPN-V2: the complete IPN-V2 architecture with an input size of 128 × 400 × 400, which means inputting the full 3D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volume.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It can be observed that the performance improves as the input size increases, suggesting that larger inputs can pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vide more global features that are beneficial for segmentation. With model parameters and GPU memory usage less than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: IPN, IPN-V2 segmented the entire OCTA volume at one time and achieved more than 10% mIoU improvement.

layout_dets.text: SEGMENTATION TASKS ON OCTA-500

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We consider each segmentation label provided by OCTA-500 as a separate segmentation task, including large vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation, capillary segmentation, artery segmentation, vein segmentation, FAZ segmentation, 3D FAZ segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion, and retinal layer segmentation. We evaluate the performance of different methods on these tasks. For large vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation, capillary segmentation, artery segmentation, vein segmentation, and FAZ segmentation, we use the base-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lines, parameter settings and evaluation metrics in this paper; for 3D FAZ segmentation, we use the baselines, parameter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: settings and evaluation metrics in (Xu et al., 2022); for retinal layer segmentation, we use the baselines, parameter settings

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and evaluation metrics in (Yang et al., 2022). All experiments are implemented on two subsets of OCTA-500, OCTA_6mm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and OCTA_3mm, respectively, using the division of training set, validation set, and test set in Section 5.1. Tables S4-S10

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provide quantitative evaluations of the test set. In the tasks of artery segmentation and vein segmentation, the IPN model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is difficult to converge during training, so this result is omitted.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Note that, the capillary segmentation, artery segmentation, and vein segmentation here differ from the corresponding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subtasks in the CAVF task: the capillaries in the CAVF task exclude arteries and veins; the arteries and veins in the CAVF

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: task intersect. The connections and differences between different tasks can be seen intuitively in Fig. S1, which provides

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: several segmentation examples using IPN-V2 in different tasks. In Fig. S2-S6, we also provide precision-recall curves of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: large vessel segmentation, capillary segmentation, artery segmentation, vein segmentation, and FAZ segmentation, from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which we can more intuitively observe the segmentation performance of different models in these tasks.

layout_dets.text: EVALUATION OF COMPARATIVE EXPERIMENTS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To facilitate researchers to query more evaluation indicators, we present the evaluation of Dice, accuracy, sensitivity and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specificity in the CAVF task in Tables S11-S14. Table 15 provides the speed evaluation of different baselines. The 2D-to-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2D baselines use less GPU memory for training and show faster testing than the 3D-to-2D baselines because a 3D-to-2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network takes more time to read the 3D volumes, and convolution on a 3D volume also requires more memory. None-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: theless, benefiting from our optimization, IPN-V2 has achieved test speeds close to 2D baselines. IPN-V2 completed the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: test with at least 2 subjects in 1 second, which is an acceptable speed. Note that, the 2D baselines take the projection maps

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as input, and the generation of the projection maps relies on layer segmentation. If the time for layer segmentation is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: considered, the 2D baselines will be slower than IPN-V2.
